_note: The four departments. Dissatisfied factions slow output and become sabotage-prone; satisfied factions are reliable and will warn the player about brewing trouble early. Each holds a board seat, so faction satisfaction and board doubt are related but distinct pressures.

factions.name: Cultivation
factions.agenda: Protect growing space and resist converting Cultivation slots to anything else
factions.warningBehaviour: Flags a failing crop a full cycle before the shortfall lands

factions.name: Engineering
factions.agenda: Keep the maintenance economy funded; resent being asked to run equipment past its condition thresholds
factions.sabotageBehaviour: Work-to-rule; repairs take the maximum allowable time
factions.warningBehaviour: Names the specific building that will break next
factions._note: The faction with the most leverage, because the maintenance economy runs thirty days behind the visible one. Their warnings are the player's only early sight of it.

factions.name: Order
factions.agenda: Expand enforcement authority; treat Freedom as a risk surface
factions.sabotageBehaviour: Selective enforcement — laws they dislike stop being applied
factions.warningBehaviour: Reports named agitators before unrest crosses the threshold
factions._note: The only faction whose satisfaction condition is partly ANTI-correlated with a meter the player wants high. Keeping Order happy and keeping Freedom high are structurally in tension.

factions.name: Archive
factions.agenda: Preserve the record and resist restrictions on access to it
factions.sabotageBehaviour: Records go missing; investigation leads cost more Focus
factions._note: Gates the investigation thread. An angry Archive makes the story itself more expensive to uncover, which is a sharper punishment than a production penalty.
